summary: CrescentBank end-of-day embeddings drift + dedicated autoscaler oscillation — priority-account escalation
description:
Issue summary:
CrescentBank reported a late-night production incident during their EOD batch where embedding similarity scores degraded sharply for their fraud-detection feature. Simultaneously, the Dedicated GPU autoscaler in the customer's reserved pool entered an oscillation loop, repeatedly adding and removing nodes. The combined effect caused increased token/embedding compute usage, streaming degrade for related endpoints, and a billing delta exposure for the customer.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: Fraud-match confidence dropped by ~30% for 2.5 hours (affecting nightly reconciliation).
- Availability: Embeddings requests experienced elevated p95 latency (1.8s -> 6.2s) and intermittent 503 from serving-runtime.
- Billing: Estimated compute overage during the incident window ~+18% above expected committed capacity.
- Business: Priority enterprise customer (CrescentBank) escalated via CSM and legal touchpoint at 22:10 UTC.

Environment:
- Dedicated Redwood pool for CrescentBank in us-east, committed capacity: 8xA10G GPUs.
- Production embedding pipeline: batch EOD job + streaming inference API.
- Model variants in rotation: redwood-embed-1.0 (primary), open-embed-xl-v2 (fallback).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Run CrescentBank nightly batch (job id RB-20260310-EOD) which issues ~1.2M embedding requests over 15 minutes.
2) Autoscaler scale-up triggers when pool utilization > 85%, provisioning new nodes.
3) Shortly after new nodes become ready, controller observed a subset of gRPC connections failing TLS handshake then reconnecting; autoscaler interpreted higher queueing and rebalanced, removing a recently added node.
4) Serving-runtime KV cache warmed on first nodes; node churn caused cache miss amplification, boosting latency and model path diversity (falling back to open-embed-xl-v2 for ~12% of requests).
5) Similarity score distribution shifted; customers noticed lower match rates.

Logs & evidence:
- Cloud metrics: autoscaler scale events spike between 21:50–23:00 UTC (see grafana/dashboard/autoscale-CrescentBank).
- Serving logs: repeated TLS handshake errors on node pool sockets (log excerpt: "tls: handshake error: EOF"), followed by connection resets and gRPC retry messages.
- Model routing traces: ~12% routed to open-embed-xl-v2 during window (trace IDs attached in related PR).
- Billing alert: billing-engine reported a delta event at 23:05 UTC (billing-alert-975310).

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Under heavy EOD batch, autoscaler oscillated due to edge-case where newly provisioned nodes briefly failed healthchecks because of an internal TLS renegotiation bug in the node image (observed handshake EOF).
- Hypothesis 2: Cache-warm jitter + route fallback increased cost and reduced embedding quality because fallback model's embedding space has systematically different cosine thresholds.
- Evidence: Kernel of TLS handshake errors correlated with a node image rollout (image tag redwood-node:v20260309-hotfix). We saw 7/8 added nodes show handshake errors in first 30s then recovery after restart.
- Temporary mitigation: pinned CrescentBank pool to older node image v20260305-rc which eliminated handshake errors on subsequent add events.

Customer communication timeline:
- 22:12 UTC: CSM Alex Chen notified support via urgent channel.
- 22:25 UTC: Initial triage with SRE oncall; acknowledged and escalated to eng.
- 23:10 UTC: Temporary mitigation (pin node image) applied; customer asked for impact quantification and credit proposal.
- 03:00 UTC (next day): Follow-up with detailed timeline and preliminary root-cause shared.

Resolution and follow-up actions:
- Root cause: Node image (redwood-node:v20260309-hotfix) introduced a TLS renegotiation race under rapid attach/detach leading to transient handshake EOFs; autoscaler interpreted transient queues as sustained demand and oscillated. This caused cache misses and model fallback amplification.
- Fix deployed: rollback node image for the dedicated pool (applied 23:05 UTC) and patched node image with TLS backoff fix in PR github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/4812.
- Billing remediation: Approved provisional credit to CrescentBank for compute delta; finance ticket INT-88421 created to reconcile final invoice.
- Long-term: Autoscaler threshold tuning and a node healthcheck grace period to avoid reacting to first-30s instability (design doc created: related_confluence_pages).

Post-incident items (owner assignments included):
- ENG-Runbook update (Jordan Patel): add 60s node warm window in autoscaler config — due 2026-03-17.
- SRE (Priya Nair): harden TLS handshake logging and add alert for handshake-EOF spike — due 2026-03-14.
- Billing/CS (Alex Chen + Finance): finalize credit and customer letter — due 2026-03-15.
- Product (Maya Lopez): review model fallback routing thresholds to avoid fallback for embeddings with known embedding-space mismatch — due 2026-03-24.
resolution_notes: Pinned customer's dedicated pool to stable node image (v20260305-rc) to stop TLS handshake failures and autoscaler oscillation. Rolled patch to node image to add TLS backoff and retry handling; updated autoscaler to include 60s warm grace period. Customer offered provisional compute credit; finance to finalize. Incident declared resolved after two clean EOD runs (2026-03-11 & 2026-03-12).
